description:
Add support for Pydantic Monty - a minimal, secure Python interpreter written in Rust for safe AI code execution.

## What is Monty?
Monty is a secure Python interpreter written in Rust by Pydantic, designed specifically for running LLM-generated code safely without the overhead of container-based sandboxes.

## Key Features
- **Secure execution**: Completely blocks access to host environment (filesystem, env variables, network)
- **Fast startup**: <1μs from code to execution result
- **Resource control**: Can track and limit memory, allocations, stack depth, and execution time
- **Type checking**: Built-in support for modern Python type hints with ty included
- **Serialization**: Can snapshot interpreter state to bytes for persistence
- **Async support**: Can run async code on the host
- **Multi-language**: Available in Python, Rust, and JavaScript

## PyPI Package
- Package: 
- Install:  or Requirement already satisfied: pydantic-monty in /home/rohitgarud/.pyenv/versions/3.12.3/lib/python3.12/site-packages (0.0.7)

## Use Cases for agent-arsenal
1. Safe code execution for AI agents - run untrusted LLM-generated Python code securely
2. Sandbox replacement - much faster than container-based sandboxes
3. Code validation - use Monty's type checking capabilities
4. Stateful execution - serialize/resume interpreter state

## Implementation Notes
- Monty is experimental and still in development
- Cannot use third-party libraries like Pydantic
- Limited standard library support (sys, os, typing, asyncio, re, datetime coming soon)
- Class definition support is coming soon

## References
- GitHub: https://github.com/pydantic/monty
- PyPI: https://pypi.org/project/pydantic-monty/
title: Add Pydantic Monty support

description:
## Feature Request

Agent Arsenal should expose its commands as MCP (Model Context Protocol) tools for integration with other agent systems like Claude Desktop, Cursor, etc.

## Why MCP?

MCP is becoming the standard for:
1. Agent tool sharing between different AI systems
2. Standardized tool discovery and invocation
3. Type-safe tool interfaces

## Implementation Options

### Option 1: Standalone MCP Server
Run as a separate process exposing arsenal commands via MCP

### Option 2: MCP Plugin
Load as a plugin into existing MCP hosts

### Option 3: Both
Both approaches for flexibility

## Expected Behavior

When running , it would:
1. Start an MCP server on a local port or stdio
2. Expose all arsenal commands as MCP tools
3. Handle tool invocation and return results

## Example MCP Manifest
title: FEAT: Add MCP server integration for agent interoperability

description:
## Bug Description

The tldr command outputs raw ANSI escape codes instead of rendered text.

## Reproduction

usage: git [--version] [--help] [-C <path>] [-c <name>=<value>]
           [--exec-path[=<path>]] [--html-path] [--man-path] [--info-path]
           [-p | --paginate | -P | --no-pager] [--no-replace-objects] [--bare]
           [--git-dir=<path>] [--work-tree=<path>] [--namespace=<name>]
           [--super-prefix=<path>] [--config-env=<name>=<envvar>]
           <command> [<args>]

These are common Git commands used in various situations:

start a working area (see also: git help tutorial)
   clone     Clone a repository into a new directory
   init      Create an empty Git repository or reinitialize an existing one

work on the current change (see also: git help everyday)
   add       Add file contents to the index
   mv        Move or rename a file, a directory, or a symlink
   restore   Restore working tree files
   rm        Remove files from the working tree and from the index

examine the history and state (see also: git help revisions)
   bisect    Use binary search to find the commit that introduced a bug
   diff      Show changes between commits, commit and working tree, etc
   grep      Print lines matching a pattern
   log       Show commit logs
   show      Show various types of objects
   status    Show the working tree status

grow, mark and tweak your common history
   branch    List, create, or delete branches
   commit    Record changes to the repository
   merge     Join two or more development histories together
   rebase    Reapply commits on top of another base tip
   reset     Reset current HEAD to the specified state
   switch    Switch branches
   tag       Create, list, delete or verify a tag object signed with GPG

collaborate (see also: git help workflows)
   fetch     Download objects and refs from another repository
   pull      Fetch from and integrate with another repository or a local branch
   push      Update remote refs along with associated objects

'git help -a' and 'git help -g' list available subcommands and some
concept guides. See 'git help <command>' or 'git help <concept>'
to read about a specific subcommand or concept.
See 'git help git' for an overview of the system.

## Root Cause

The handler in handlers/tldr.py returns raw output without stripping ANSI codes.

## Fix Required

1. Import and use a library like strip-ansi or implement manually
2. Strip ANSI escape sequences from the tldr output before returning

Alternative: Use Rich to render properly with console.strip=False
title: BUG: tldr command outputs raw ANSI escape codes

description:
Different commands use inconsistent argument patterns, confusing for agents:

1. base64: Uses --mode encode/decode but CLI expects 'encode' as separate arg:
   - arsenal common base64 --input 'hello' --mode encode  # Works
   - echo 'hello' | arsenal common base64 encode  # FAILS

2. json: Doesn't have --mode, uses boolean flags:
   - arsenal common code json --input '{}' --validate  # Works
   - No way to specify 'format' mode explicitly

3. hash: Uses --algorithm consistently - good pattern to follow

Recommendation: Standardize on subcommand style:
- arsenal common base64 encode --input 'hello'
- arsenal common base64 decode --input 'aGVsbG8='
- arsenal common code json format --input '{}'
- arsenal common code json validate --input '{}'

- Efficient querying of virtual file metadata

- Create a new  module in src/agent_arsenal/
- Design schema for virtual files (path, content, metadata, timestamps)
- Implement CRUD operations (create, read, update, delete)
- Add transaction support for atomic operations
- Provide a clean API similar to pathlib for intuitive usage
- Consider integration with existing state management

This is related to the state management system (state.py) and could enhance caching (cache.py) capabilities.
